title: Longitudinal DLQI trajectory patterns and early risk updating in telepharmacy-monitored psoriasis.
summary: Ward clustering of psoriasis quality-of-life trajectories identified three exploratory patterns, including a persistent-burden group; for remission, month-one DLQI updating improved AUROC to 0.753 with calibration, while baseline DLQI alone matched/outperformed ensembles for improvement. This is a retrospective telepharmacy cohort result and shows limited incremental value of complex ML.
ai_technology: Ward clustering identifies DLQI trajectory groups; repeated-split machine-learning models update psoriasis-remission risk from month-one scores.
